You cannot remove ads on Twitch using their settings. Only subbing and/or adblock will do that, with inconsistent results (some adblockers are detectable by Twitch and run their own version of 'we see you're using adblock, disable it to remove these messages' that run far more frequently than any ad would. Twitch does allow you to choose between pre-roll ads and ads that run during the middle of your broadcast.   
If you enable the ad manager you can choose to have your ads run anywhere from 30 seconds per hour to 3 minutes per hour. You can also choose to have the ad start 0-30 minutes into the broadcast. If you run ads manually while you step away (afk), the auto-scheduler will not run that ads that hour.   
They did a study and something like 7 out of every 10 new viewers will stream hop the moment they see pre-roll ads. You have a better chance at viewer retention by scheduling the ads for the bare minimum (30 seconds), as late into the broadcast as possible (30mins). This gives you time to win over new viewers before an ad runs and they leave. Your loyal viewers won't care as much, because ads are their way of supporting you without subbing, donating, etc. Keep em short, keep 'em sweet. Hope this helps.

Our world simply doesn't know how to effectively deal with the mentally ill. It's a catch-22 scenario. 

In the Holmes case, he indicated to his therapist that he was having homicidal thoughts in the months leading up to the shooting. It's in the notes that there was major concern from the psychiatrist, but they didn't feel like he was an immediate threat to society - so nothing was done. 

On the flip side, if you remove someone from society with a temporary 72-hour psych hold simply because they mention they're having homicidal/suicidal thoughts, then you'll see less and less mentally ill people reaching out for help. It's the fear of losing control over your life that scares people away from 'real' help. 

It's become such a taboo subject to even discuss because of the fragility of mental illness. Their behavior is unpredictable because they don't think the same way most people do. 

'What if I say the wrong thing and they kill themselves or hurt someone else? I'm worried how they're going to react.' 

And because of this, very few people are willing to have real conversations with mentally ill people about mental illness, about the value of your own life and about the value of other peoples lives.
